draft.title: Jewish ethics
card: Jewish ethics are guided by the mitzvot, the commandments found in the Torah. Tradition counts 613 of them. A single commandment is a mitzvah.
The Ten Commandments are part of the 613. They include rules about worshipping God, honouring parents, not murdering, not stealing and not lying.
Justice is a core Jewish value. It means treating people fairly, protecting the weak and acting honestly. In Hebrew this is called tzedek.
Tikkun olam means repairing the world. It is the idea that people can improve the world through acts such as helping the poor and caring for others.
draft.remember: The mitzvot give Jewish ethics their rules, and justice and repairing the world give them their aims.

a.q: How are the Ten Commandments related to the 613 mitzvot?
opts: They are part of the 613 mitzvot
They are a separate set from the 613
They replace the 613 mitzvot
They are the 613 mitzvot in short form
a.why: The Ten Commandments are found in the Torah and are counted among the 613 mitzvot. They are not a separate set, because the 613 include them along with many other commandments.
a.clue: Think about whether ten is a part of 613 or apart from it.

b.q: Noah's family in Melbourne runs a food drive for people in need because they want to repair the world. Which Jewish value are they acting on?
opts: Tikkun olam
Mitzvah as a single rule
Shabbat observance
Covenant with Abraham
b.why: Tikkun olam means repairing the world through acts such as helping the poor. Shabbat is a different practice, and the food drive is about improving the world, not about resting.
b.clue: Look for the value whose name means repairing the world.

a.best: They are part of the 613 mitzvot

problems.detail: The remember line splits the ideas into 'rules' (mitzvot) and 'aims' (justice, repairing the world), a division the card never makes. It is also misleading, because pursuing justice is itself commanded in the Torah.

The stem says the family acts 'because they want to repair the world', which is the card's definition of tikkun olam, so the question tests matching words rather than understanding. The clue repeats the giveaway, and 'Mitzvah as a single rule' is not a value at all, so the question is too easy.
'Not lying' loosely glosses the commandment against bearing false witness against one's neighbour. A more accurate wording would be 'not giving false testimony' or 'not bearing false witness'.

proposal.title: Jewish ethics
card: Jewish ethics are guided by the mitzvot, the commandments found in the Torah. Tradition counts 613 of them. A single commandment is a mitzvah.
The Ten Commandments are part of the 613. They include worshipping only God, honouring parents, and not murdering, stealing or bearing false witness against others.
Justice, in Hebrew tzedek, means treating people fairly, protecting the weak and acting honestly. The Torah itself commands it: 'Justice, justice you shall pursue.'
Tikkun olam means repairing the world. It is the idea that people can improve the world through acts such as helping the poor and caring for others.
proposal.remember: The 613 mitzvot, including the Ten Commandments, guide Jewish life, along with values such as justice and tikkun olam.

a.q: How are the Ten Commandments related to the 613 mitzvot?
opts: They are part of the 613 mitzvot
They are a separate set from the 613
They replace the other 613 mitzvot
They are found outside the Torah
a.why: The Ten Commandments are found in the Torah and are counted among the 613 mitzvot. They are not a separate set, because the 613 include them along with many other commandments.
a.clue: Is ten a part of 613 or apart from it?

b.q: Ari's friend says justice in Judaism is only an ideal, separate from the commandments. Which reply best corrects her?
opts: The Torah itself commands Jews to pursue justice
Justice comes from the Talmud, not from the Torah
Justice replaced the mitzvot as the guide to ethics
Justice is part of tikkun olam, not the mitzvot
b.why: The Torah says 'Justice, justice you shall pursue', so justice is both a value and a commandment. Calling it part of tikkun olam is tempting, as both aim to improve life for others, but that does not show it is commanded.
b.clue: Where does the call to pursue justice come from?
